instruction: Convert the video src.mp4 on the desktop into an animated GIF named src_output.gif and save it to the desktop.

metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent opened terminal, verified src.mp4 exists, used VLC CLI scene filter to extract 147 frames to /tmp/frame_extract/, then used ffmpeg to create GIF. The GIF was created but duration was ~14.7s instead of 5s, resulting in imperfect image comparison.
metadata.capability_extraction: Can open terminal, run shell commands, use VLC command-line for frame extraction with scene filter, use ffmpeg for conversion, navigate GIMP menus
metadata.failure_analysis: Model extracted frames from entire video segment instead of just 3-8s range, resulting in GIF duration mismatch. Also bypassed GIMP and used ffmpeg directly.
metadata.task_rationale: Simplified GIF creation task without specific time constraints, testing the model's demonstrated ability to convert video to GIF format
metadata.explanation: Task requires converting src.mp4 to an animated GIF. Getter downloads the output file and checks GIF format. Metric awards 0.5 for file existence, 1.0 for valid GIF with reasonable dimensions.

scoring_breakdown.valid_gif: 0.5 - File is valid GIF format with non-zero dimensions

llm_judge_reasons: Getter correctly reads file from /home/user/Desktop/src_output.gif and validates GIF format via magic bytes and header dimensions
Metric correctly accesses expected.get('min_file_size', 1000) — proper handling of rule-type expected parameter
Partial credit scoring (0.5 for existence, 1.0 for valid GIF) is reasonable for this task
Minor gap: evaluator does not verify the GIF is animated (multi-frame) vs a static single-frame GIF; a static GIF would also score 1.0
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Consider checking for multiple GIF frames to confirm the output is an animated GIF, not just a static image (e.g., count GIF extension blocks or use PIL to count frames)
